newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity closes off on ample power supply.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity closes off on ample power supply.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures prices closed lower Friday in lackluster activity, pressured by plentiful power supplies in the western U.S., trade sources said.
"The outlook for hydroelectricity is supporting lower out-month prices," said one trader.
Above-normal rain and snowfall so far this winter in both the Pacific Northwest and northern California is expected to result in abundant hydropower supplies through spring and early summer.
Market sources also cited holiday absences, weaker natural gas prices and mild weather as contributing to today's slow tone for power futures.
February 1997 COB futures closed down 93 cents per megawatt hour (MWh) at $15.24, while the March contract finished 80 cents lower at $13.70. Other active COB contracts were 70 cents to $1.00 lower.
February Palo Verde settled down 56 cents at $16.44, while March ended 80 cents lower at $15.50. Other PV contracts were five to 80 cents lower.
NYMEX said 113 COB contracts traded, while 56 PV lots changed hands.
